evidence_set: The review prints 89% female and infers probable female predisposition from its case table. Editors' recount is 46/52=88.4615%, or 88.5% to one decimal; this differs from the printed 89%, with no alternate author denominator inferred. If two probable duplicate female rows are omitted, the conditional recount is 44/50=88.0%, not a verified distinct-patient sample. No number of female and male people who take MDMA is set against those selected cases, so these shares do not estimate susceptibility.
Table 3 sex/reference columns (pp. 5–6); Section 5 female-share inference (p. 7); Matthai/Wilkins reference entries (p. 14); editorial calculations.

The review reports that, once hyponatraemic encephalopathy develops, menstruant women were about 25 times as likely to die or have permanent brain injury as men or postmenopausal women (Ayus 1992). The reference title on p.12 identifies postoperative patients, not people who take MDMA. Other proposed hormonal and muscle-mass explanations are drawn from physiology/animal work rather than a test of those explanations in people taking MDMA; primary reports were not read.
Section 5.1.5 second and third paragraphs (pp. 10–11); Ayus 1992 postoperative-encephalopathy reference entry (p. 12).
